title: Encoding of a circuit difference
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $C$ and $C'$ be arithmetic circuits over $n$ input variables. Suppose the first and second components parsed from $x$ decode, respectively, to the indexed circuits $(n,C)$ and $(n,C')$. Assume each circuit is nonempty and every gate referring to earlier gates refers only to gates with smaller indices. Then the string produced by the circuit-difference construction on $x$ is the encoding of the circuit formed by appending the gates of $C'$, with their references shifted by the size of $C$, to the gates of $C$, followed by a subtraction gate whose inputs are the outputs of $C$ and the shifted copy of $C'$.
hypotheses_covered: The first parsed component of $x$ decodes to $(n,C)$

Every gate reference in $C$ points to an earlier gate
Every gate reference in $C'$ points to an earlier gate
